idea.title: Why a comet's tail points away from the Sun
idea.description: The tail is not a wake: what pushes it.

shots.visual: a comet moving away from the Sun, tail ahead
shots.narration: This comet you are looking at right now is on its way out, leaving the Sun behind it. And, strangely enough, its long tail is out in front of it, leading the way.
shots.shows: the tail leads the comet outward

shots.visual: the same stream reaching Earth, a city's lights going out
shots.narration: A tail that leads the way instead of trailing behind? Whatever it is that is pushing that tail out ahead reaches you too, right here at home. In March 1989 a storm in it put the power out across Quebec for nine long hours.
shots.shows: the stream that bends the tail arrives at Earth

shots.narration: So the question is a simple one to ask: what, exactly, is pushing it?
Sunlight itself pushes on things. Not by very much at all, but on something as small as a grain of dust it turns out to be enough.

shots.visual: a straight gas tail beside a curved dust tail
shots.narration: But a comet does not have just the one tail. It has a second tail, made of gas, and that one is straight, and it is fast. It is far, far too fast for sunlight alone to explain.
shots.shows: the gas tail outruns the dust tail

shots.visual: the two tails, the straight one highlighted
shots.narration: In 1951 a scientist named Ludwig Biermann asked what seems, looking back on it, the obvious question: if it is not the light, then what else is blowing?

shots.visual: particles streaming out from the Sun past a comet
shots.narration: His answer was this: the Sun never stops shedding itself, not for a moment. A steady stream of particles pours out of it, in every direction, all of the time, without a pause.
shots.shows: particles leaving the Sun and bending the gas tail

shots.narration: Eleven years later the Mariner 2 probe flew right through that stream and measured it directly. Today we call it the solar wind.
So now, with all of that in mind, look again at that comet from the very beginning.

shots.visual: the opening comet, the stream visible
shots.narration: It is not flying backwards at all. What it is doing is showing you the wind.
shots.shows: the tail pointing along the stream
